questions.question: What does $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to x_0}f(x) = L$ mean informally?
In the $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ definition of a limit at a point, which condition keeps $x$ in a punctured neighbourhood of $x_0$?
Which example is a limit at a point?
For $f(x) = x^2$, what is the listed value of $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0}f(x)$?
Why does the definition assume that $f$ is defined whenever $0 \lt |x-x_0| \lt r$ for some $r \gt 0$?
options: So the domain must be all of $\mathbb{R}$.
So the limit must be infinite

questions.question: If the limit of a function at a point exists, can it have two different values?
options: If a limit exists, it is unique
Every function has a limit at every point
A limit exists only when $f(x_0)$ is defined
Two different limits may exist at the same point

questions.question: Assume $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to x_0}f(x) = L$. What must happen for every $\varepsilon \gt 0$?
options: There is a $\delta \lt 0$ such that $x = x_0$ implies $f(x) = L$
There is an $r \lt 0$ such that $f$ is undefined near $x_0$
There is an $L$ such that $|x-L| \lt \varepsilon$ for all $x$
There is a $\delta \gt 0$ such that $0 \lt |x-x_0| \lt \delta$ implies $|f(x)-L| \lt \varepsilon$

questions.question: A function is not defined at $x_0$, but it is defined for all nearby $x\ne x_0$ and approaches $L$. Which statement is consistent?
options: The limit must equal $f(x_0)$ by definition
The function may still have limit $L$ at $x_0$

questions.question: Evaluate $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to1}\frac{x^2-1}{x-1}$ (the expression is undefined at $x=1$).
What is $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\sin x}{x}$?
A student proposes to prove $\lim_{x\to x_0}f(x) = L$ by checking only $x = x_0$. What is wrong with this approach?
options: The definition requires checking only integer values of $x$
The definition says $\varepsilon$ must be negative

questions.question: Suppose a claimed proof uses a $\delta$ with $\delta \gt r$, where $r$ is the radius on which $f$ is known to be defined around $x_0$. Which safer adjustment matches the definition?
In $\lim_{x\to x_0}f(x)=L$, what is being controlled by $\varepsilon$?
For $f(x)=\dfrac{|x|}{x}$ (with $x\ne0$), does $\lim_{x\to0}f(x)$ exist?
In the $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ definition, how must the chosen $\delta$ typically respond as $\varepsilon$ is made smaller?
options: A smaller $\varepsilon$ generally forces a smaller $\delta$
$\delta$ does not depend on $\varepsilon$ at all

questions.question: What is $\lim_{x\to 0}(x^2+x)$?
For $f(x)=5$ when $x\ne 2$, what is $\lim_{x\to2}f(x)$?
A function has $\lim_{x\to2}f(x)=5$ but $f(2)=1$. Is this possible?
options: Yes; the limit depends on nearby values, not on $f(2)$
No; $f$ cannot be defined at $2$ in that case

questions.question: Does $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\frac{1}{x^2}$ exist as a real number?
options: No; the values grow beyond every bound
Yes; it equals a finite real number

questions.question: If $\lim_{x\to x_0}f(x)=4$, what must hold for $\varepsilon=0.01$?
options: There must be no $x$ close to $x_0$.
